name: Cervical Central Cord Syndrome
definition: Incomplete cervical spinal cord injury classically causing greater weakness in the upper limbs than lower limbs, often after hyperextension trauma in a stenotic cervical canal.

typical: Upper-limb weakness greater than leg weakness

investigations.principle: CT assesses fracture; MRI assesses cord edema, compression, disc and ligament injury.
investigations.MRI: Use MRI when neural, soft-tissue, marrow, inflammatory, infection, occult injury or other condition-specific assessment requires it.
investigations.radiographs: Use radiographs and/or CT according to the condition-specific imaging pathway.

amber: Surgical decompression is individualized according to compression, instability and neurological status.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Any Pakshaghata/Vata framework is secondary to modern spinal cord injury care.

patientEducation.summary: Incomplete cervical spinal cord injury classically causing greater weakness in the upper limbs than lower limbs, often after hyperextension trauma in a stenotic cervical canal.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute/progressive neurological deficit, sphincter change, severe infection/systemic illness, major trauma, vascular compromise or other listed red flags.
